name: ripgrep
summary: Exact symbol and text search across tracked trees.
why: Fast, ignore-aware, and sufficient for targeted context. `eng impact` uses it for reference discovery.
failure_mode: Finds text, not meaning: misses dynamic references, macros and generated code.

name: git grep
summary: Search tracked files without extra tooling.
why: Portable fallback when ripgrep is unavailable; matches the exact revision in Git.
failure_mode: Same textual limits as ripgrep; untracked files are invisible to it.

name: Language servers
summary: Compiler-backed definitions, references and diagnostics.
why: The most reliable symbol lookup when the language server is configured. Use it before text search for ambiguous symbols.
failure_mode: Only as good as the project's build configuration; a stale index or failing build gives wrong answers.

name: Cargo metadata
summary: Build graph, package names and targets without reading the tree.
why: The authoritative Rust workspace graph; safer than directory guesses.
failure_mode: Describes the declared graph, not feature-gated or build-script-generated code paths.

name: ast-grep
summary: Structural search and rewrite across many languages.
why: Useful when text search cannot distinguish a definition from a call site. Not adopted until false negatives are measured on real changes.
failure_mode: Rules match syntax, not types; a pattern can silently miss variants.

name: tree-sitter
summary: Incremental parsing for structural indexes.
why: A foundation for symbol extraction, but adds grammars and build surface. Current impact analysis is explicitly textual.
failure_mode: Grammars lag language releases; parse errors degrade to partial trees.

name: SCIP / LSIF
summary: Persistent code-intelligence indexes for large repositories.
why: Would improve cross-repository navigation; not justified until a repository's text search is measurably insufficient.
failure_mode: Indexes go stale between builds; a stale index reports outdated references.

name: cargo test / nextest
summary: Rust unit, integration and doc tests.
why: Native, deterministic and already the merge condition in Rust repositories.
failure_mode: Proves only what the tests assert; feature flags and targets not built are not tested.

name: pytest
summary: Python unit and integration tests.
why: Native framework with fixtures and parametrization; used only when the repository declares it.
failure_mode: Fixtures and monkeypatching can hide real integration failures.

name: node:test / Vitest
summary: JavaScript and TypeScript tests.
why: Prefer the framework already declared by the repository; do not add a second runner.
failure_mode: Mocks and test environments (jsdom) differ from real runtimes.

name: swift test
summary: Swift package tests on macOS and Linux.
why: Native SwiftPM test runner; required for Swift packages.
failure_mode: Simulator and host differ from devices; UI behaviour needs separate tests.

name: Gradle test
summary: JVM and Android unit/instrumentation tests.
why: Authoritative for Gradle projects; instrumentation tests need a device or emulator.
failure_mode: Robolectric and emulators differ from devices; instrumentation tests can be flaky.

name: Property-based testing (proptest)
summary: Generate inputs from invariants instead of enumerating examples.
why: High value for parsers, math kernels and state machines. Add per repository with a shrinking corpus and a deterministic seed.
failure_mode: Generators can miss the interesting region; an unpinned seed makes failures hard to reproduce.

name: Fuzzing (cargo-fuzz)
summary: Coverage-guided input exploration for parsers and binary formats.
why: Needed for hostile input surfaces. Requires a corpus, a crash triage process and a time budget; not a default fast check.
failure_mode: Finds only what the harness reaches; no crashes in a short run is weak evidence.

name: Mutation testing (cargo-mutants)
summary: Test the tests by mutating production code.
why: Useful evidence that a test suite detects faults; expensive and language-specific, so run it on critical modules rather than every commit.
failure_mode: Slow, and surviving equivalent mutants create noise; easy to misread as a coverage score.

name: Golden and snapshot tests (insta)
summary: Freeze serialized output, CLI text, rendering and formats.
why: Strong contract evidence when the golden files are reviewed and regenerated deliberately, never to make a red test green.
failure_mode: Regenerating goldens to make a red test green turns them into rubber stamps.

name: Contract and differential tests
summary: Old/new fixtures and reference implementations for compatibility.
why: Required for public APIs, schemas, persistence and protocols. A contract claim without a fixture is an opinion.
failure_mode: Fixtures cover the cases someone thought of; real consumers may rely on others.

name: gitleaks
summary: Secret scanning for tracked files and history.
why: High-signal maintained rules. The kit scans a hard-linked tracked tree, so build output is never scanned.
failure_mode: Pattern-based: misses novel secret formats and flags fake ones; untracked files are not scanned.

name: Semgrep CE
summary: Language-aware SAST with a small, tested rule set.
why: Runs locally and in CI, supports custom rules and fixtures. Eight baseline rules cover command injection, TLS, YAML, pickle and execSync.
failure_mode: Only the rules configured; a clean run means those rules found nothing.

name: OSV-Scanner
summary: Dependency vulnerabilities from lockfiles.
why: Uses OSV data, requires no account and works with Cargo.lock and other ecosystems. Findings are never suppressed to make a gate green.
failure_mode: Needs network and a supported lockfile; advisories lag disclosure.

name: actionlint
summary: GitHub Actions syntax, expression and shell checks.
why: Catches workflow mistakes before merge and works on every workflow file.
failure_mode: Checks syntax and shell, not whether a workflow is safe to run on untrusted input.

name: zizmor
summary: Security audit for GitHub Actions workflows.
why: Finds template injection, credential persistence and unpinned actions. The platform and kit run it as a gate.
failure_mode: Static audit of workflow files; cannot see repository settings or secrets scoping.

name: CodeQL
summary: Deep dataflow and semantic code analysis.
why: Strong for scheduled deep analysis, but heavier and GitHub-hosted. Semgrep remains the fast local gate; add CodeQL where its dataflow adds measured value.
failure_mode: Slow and heavy; query coverage varies by language, and alerts need triage.

name: Trivy / Grype / Syft
summary: Image, filesystem, SBOM and vulnerability scanning.
why: Adopt when a release produces container images or archives. The current pilot has no such artifact.
failure_mode: Database freshness and noise; image scans miss what is fetched at runtime.

name: Cosign
summary: Sign and verify release artifacts and attestations.
why: Only useful once there is an artifact and a signing policy. `release-check` can verify a supplied signature; it does not create keys or sign.
failure_mode: A signature proves who signed, not that the artifact is safe; key or identity mistakes break trust.

name: Git worktrees
summary: One checkout and branch per independent unit.
why: Native isolation with no extra service. The eng CLI records ownership and a concurrency cap.
failure_mode: Isolate files, not shared caches, ports, databases or devices.

name: eng CLI
summary: Detect, impact, verify, guard, security, worktrees and evidence.
why: A dependency-free control plane that gives humans, agents and CI the same answers.
failure_mode: Runs what the config says; a weak config gives a green gate that proves little.

name: GitHub Actions
summary: Shared, immutable quality gates and evidence artifacts.
why: The existing CI system. Add a verify step to it; do not replace working pipelines. Pin every action to a commit SHA.
failure_mode: A pull request runs its own copy of the workflow, so CI cannot vouch for changes to CI.

name: Containers
summary: Ephemeral, reproducible execution where native setup is insufficient.
why: Useful for cross-platform builds and hostile fixtures. Do not add a container runtime when a local process is adequate.
failure_mode: Image drift and unpinned bases break reproducibility; containers are not a strong security boundary on their own.

name: sccache (S3-compatible)
summary: Shared compiler cache for Rust (and C/C++) across runners, on S3-compatible storage.
why: High value for large Rust workspaces. Only main-branch CI gets write credentials; PR builds and agents read. Separate prefixes per project and toolchain; never put credentials in the repository.
install: cargo install sccache (or a pinned CI action)
failure_mode: A poisoned or mismatched cache returns wrong artifacts; key mismatches (paths, flags, toolchain) give near-zero hit rates.

name: Evidence records
summary: Hash-chained JSON for every verification run.
why: The audit unit. Records commands, exit codes, durations, output hashes, Git state and scanner versions; skipped is never pass.
failure_mode: Local and unsigned: proves integrity of the chain, not who produced it.

name: CI artifacts
summary: Retain evidence outside the agent's context.
why: CI uploads `.agents/evidence/` even when the gate fails, so a reviewer can inspect the failing log after the runner is gone.
failure_mode: Retention expires; artifacts are only as trustworthy as the job that uploaded them.

name: OpenTelemetry
summary: Traces, metrics and logs across agents and services.
why: Adopt when there is a collector and a consumer for the data. Evidence JSON is the current audit unit.
failure_mode: Instrumentation without a consumer is cost without value; traces can leak sensitive data.

name: Agent evaluation harness
summary: Scored tasks in isolated worktrees.
why: Measures pass rate, duration and diff size for any agent command. The stub validates the harness; a no-op agent must score zero.
failure_mode: Two smoke tasks: detects gross regressions, not model quality.

name: AGENTS.md
summary: The repository's authoritative policy and map.
why: One place for commands, invariants, compatibility, security and evidence rules. Skills do not duplicate it.
failure_mode: Stale policy misleads agents; it is guidance, not enforcement.

name: Agent Skills
summary: Seventeen task-specific entrypoints with workflows and completion criteria.
why: Load one skill for the task instead of injecting every instruction into every context.
failure_mode: Text, not enforcement: an agent can ignore a skill; the gate still has to catch it.

name: ADRs and architecture docs
summary: Durable decisions linked to source and tests.
why: Prevents stale chat summaries from overriding current code. Invalidate docs when the code they describe changes.
failure_mode: Decisions rot if not linked to code and revisited.

name: OpenCode
summary: Agent executor with skills, tools and sessions.
why: Reads AGENTS.md and `.opencode/skills`; the installer links the canonical `.agents/skills` there.
failure_mode: Executor behaviour changes between versions; its permissions must be configured, not assumed.

name: Codex CLI
summary: Agent executor and AGENTS.md reader.
why: Discovers repository policy through AGENTS.md; the CLI remains the same portable entrypoint.
failure_mode: Executor behaviour changes between versions; sandbox and approval settings vary by environment.

name: Claude Code
summary: Agent executor with project skills.
why: Reads `.claude/skills`; the installer links the canonical skill directory there.
failure_mode: Executor behaviour changes between versions; permission modes must be set deliberately.

name: Autobot
summary: Local-first agent with threads, approvals and receipts.
why: The control-plane target: one worktree per thread, durable approvals, signed gateway receipts. Not the default executor for this kit.
failure_mode: Local agent in development; receipts are only as complete as the instrumentation.

name: Invincible gateway
summary: Model gateway with policy, redaction, receipts and audit.
why: The agent should receive a gateway token, not provider keys. Keep it loopback/private and inject credentials at runtime.
failure_mode: Gateway in development; a misconfigured policy can pass or block more than intended.

name: LiteLLM
summary: Self-hosted model routing and budgets.
why: Centralizes provider keys and model policy. Requires the platform environment and budget configuration.
failure_mode: Another service to run and secure; routing errors can send data to the wrong provider.

name: GitHub
summary: Issues, PRs, CI runs, artifacts and checks.
why: The shared collaboration and enforcement surface. Use least-privilege tokens; never commit them.
failure_mode: Platform outages and rate limits; API tokens are high-value credentials.

name: Plane
summary: Work items, projects and delivery tracking.
why: Use when the repository's policy requires the work item to track the change. It does not authorize code changes.
failure_mode: Tracking drifts from reality unless items are updated when work lands.

name: pen.dev / Pencil
summary: Design files and rendered UI artifacts.
why: Use for UI design work when the task is visual. It does not replace code, tests or accessibility review.
failure_mode: Design files drift from shipped UI without a review step.

name: cargo-nextest
summary: Faster Rust test runner: per-test processes, retries reported, JUnit output.
why: Usually faster than cargo test on large workspaces. Does not run doctests; keep `cargo test --doc` in the gate.
failure_mode: Skips doctests unless run separately; retries can hide flakes if they are treated as passes.

name: mold or lld
summary: A faster linker for large Rust binaries.
why: Linking often dominates incremental Rust builds. Measure with and without; mold is Linux-focused, lld is cross-platform.
failure_mode: Platform-specific flags; a linker difference can surface as an obscure link error or a different binary layout.

name: cargo-hakari
summary: Workspace-hack crate so feature unification stops causing rebuilds.
why: Helps large workspaces whose crates rebuild because features differ between builds. Adds a generated crate to maintain.
command: cargo hakari generate && cargo hakari verify
failure_mode: A stale workspace-hack causes surprising rebuilds or feature changes; it must be verified in CI.

name: cargo-chef
summary: Caches Rust dependency builds as a container layer.
why: Useful when CI builds in Docker and dependency compilation dominates. Not needed with a working compiler cache.
command: cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json && cargo chef cook --release --recipe-path recipe.json
failure_mode: Only helps container builds; a recipe out of sync with the lockfile caches the wrong dependencies.

name: bacon
summary: Background checker for the local Rust inner loop.
why: Keeps check/clippy/test feedback running while editing. A developer convenience, not evidence: results are not recorded.
failure_mode: Its output is not evidence; a green bacon pane is not a verified gate.

name: cargo-deny
summary: Licence, advisory, source and duplicate-version checks for Rust dependencies.
why: Belongs in the required gate of Rust repositories with a reviewed deny.toml. Exceptions are narrow and dated.
failure_mode: A permissive deny.toml or broad exceptions make it pass without checking; needs the advisory database (network).

name: cargo-audit
summary: RustSec advisory scan of Cargo.lock.
why: Overlaps with cargo-deny advisories and OSV; use one consistently and keep it in the required gate.
failure_mode: Advisories lag disclosure; ignored IDs must carry a reason and an expiry.

name: cargo-machete
summary: Finds unused dependencies in Cargo.toml.
why: Fast and dependency-free; unused dependencies cost build time and attack surface.
failure_mode: Text-based: false positives for dependencies used only through macros or build scripts.

name: cargo-llvm-cov
summary: Source-based code coverage for Rust tests.
why: Shows untested code paths in a change. Coverage is a map of what ran, not a quality score.
failure_mode: High coverage with weak assertions proves little; instrumented builds are slower and can change timing.

name: Nix / devenv
summary: Declarative, pinned development and CI environments.
why: Makes 'works on my machine' reproducible across agents and runners. Steep learning curve; adopt when environment drift is a measured problem.
failure_mode: Complexity and evaluation time; macOS support differs from Linux.

name: mise
summary: Pinned tool versions per repository (toolchains, CLIs).
why: Lighter than Nix for pinning tool versions; does not pin system libraries.
failure_mode: Pins tools, not the OS or system libraries; plugins fetch from the network.

name: Dagger
summary: CI pipelines as code that run the same locally and in CI.
why: Useful when pipelines must run identically on laptops, agents and CI. Adds an engine to run and secure.
failure_mode: Another runtime in the trust path; engine caching needs the same poisoning care as build caches.

name: gVisor
summary: User-space kernel sandbox for containers running untrusted work.
why: Stronger isolation than a plain container for agent tasks on untrusted code.
failure_mode: Syscall compatibility gaps and performance overhead for I/O-heavy builds.

name: Firecracker
summary: MicroVMs for strong per-task isolation.
why: VM-level isolation with fast start-up; suits running many untrusted agent tasks on one host.
failure_mode: Linux/KVM only; image, network and storage plumbing is yours to build and secure.

name: Buck2 or Bazel (remote execution)
summary: Hermetic builds with remote caching and execution.
why: Only worth it at a scale where Cargo plus a compiler cache is measurably not enough. Large migration cost.
failure_mode: Migration cost and a second build definition that can drift from Cargo; hermeticity breaks quietly.

name: Temporal
summary: Durable workflows for long-running, retryable agent orchestration.
why: Consider when agent pipelines need durable retries and state across failures. A service to operate.
failure_mode: A stateful service to run, secure and upgrade; workflow code has determinism rules that are easy to break.

name: Langfuse-style agent traces
summary: Traces of agent runs: prompts, tool calls, cost and latency.
why: Helps find stalled or expensive agents. Traces contain prompts and code; treat them as confidential.
failure_mode: Traces can capture secrets and private code; another data store to secure and retain correctly.

name: Prometheus / Grafana
summary: Metrics and dashboards for CI duration, queue depth, cache hit rate and cost.
why: Adopt when the improvement loop needs trends that evidence files alone do not show.
failure_mode: Dashboards nobody reads; metrics without definitions drift from references/metrics.md.

name: Push notifications for exceptions
summary: Deliver the exception digest to the human who owns it.
why: Attention is scarce: push only `eng digest` items, never every pass.
failure_mode: Alert fatigue if it sends passes; silent failure if the notifier breaks, so a missing digest must itself be noticed.

name: KiCad with KiBot
summary: Schematic/PCB design with scripted ERC/DRC and fabrication outputs.
why: Makes hardware design checks reproducible in CI. Not exercised in any WCKD repository with recorded evidence.
failure_mode: Rule checks only cover the rules configured; generated outputs must not be hand-edited.

name: ngspice
summary: Circuit simulation (SPICE).
why: Checks power, sensing and driver circuits before fabrication. Results are only as good as the device models.
failure_mode: Wrong or idealised models give confident wrong answers.

name: Renode / QEMU
summary: Emulate microcontrollers and boards to test firmware without devices.
why: Runs firmware tests in CI before a bench. Peripheral models are incomplete.
failure_mode: Missing or inaccurate peripheral models; timing differs from hardware.

name: MuJoCo
summary: Physics simulation for robot controllers.
why: Tests gaits and controllers in simulation with fixed seeds before hardware.
failure_mode: Sim-to-real gap: contact, friction and actuator models differ from the robot.

name: Hardware-in-the-loop runner
summary: A self-hosted runner attached to real devices for bench tests.
why: The last step after simulation and emulation. Needs safe test sequences and human approval for anything that can damage hardware.
failure_mode: Untrusted code on a runner with physical devices; flaky hardware reported as passing.
